note: IEEPA refunds very likely land in the Aug-Oct quarter and are not in a consensus down 9% y/y on sales now known to be up (peers TJX and Levi booked large ones), but it is a one-off on a name that sold a one-off-driven beat at -9.1% in Q1, and the 13% inventory build cuts the other way; sales are pre-released monthly so the move scale is small, not the 13.7% a 47%-wide chain implies.

Webull's own June monthly operating data plus the CEO's July/August commentary imply a Q3 options run-rate well above a bar asking only +8-12% q/q revenue, and HOOD (the closest peer, reporting after Webull last spoke) printed options contracts +17% q/q; the Cboe industry series and the House China overhang on first-time Q4-to-date flow disclosure are what keep it modest.

The FY27 revenue consensus of $1.72B looks to carry only part of Megger's ~$590M, so a first combined guide near $1.95-2.05B screens as a large beat; almost entirely offset because the bar has one source, scope is seen through by real holders, Woodward guided FY27 soft the day before and was sold, and ESE has sold its last two prints (-8.9%, -6.8%) including a beat-and-raise.

The reaction function this season is the finding: Datadog and Dynatrace both beat and fell 14-16% on their guides, ESTC's own Nov 2025 beat-and-raise fell 14.7%, and the bar here is already a beat (whisper $0.88 against a $0.80-0.82 guide top); TD Cowen's 11-17 cautious observability channel checks and Cisco's +2% observability line are the only genuinely new information and both point down, with the Anthropic IPO keeping sector pressure inside the window.

Three tanker peers that reported the same quarter after Frontline last spoke beat enormously (ECO $7.67 vs $4.84, DHT +29%, INSW revenue +22%) and were bought in the same falling-rate tape (DHT +4.9%, ECO +3.6%), while FRO's consensus still sits below Q2's $2.61 adjusted EPS and the dividend tracks EPS plus an $0.80 special; discounted for the 64% VLCC spot collapse that the Q4/Q1 commentary will be struck at, and the +23 skew is read off a chain whose own baseline says the 82% spread means nothing.

The company quantified a $35M Section 301 benefit conditional on the 10% rate holding through Q3-end, the condition appears met, and full-year consensus of $2.33 sits BELOW the guide low of $2.35, so the street has not taken it; Q2 is the template (sales miss, EPS beat and raise, +12.9%), the crowded long UBS flagged has been hit by 12.6% since, and the UBS traffic data and warm-weather apparel reads are the offset.

25.5% of shares out short and 10.65 days to cover into a print where the bear case (flat Q4, possible 2027 decline) was published by Guggenheim on 11-11 and sold into, with calls bid at -29.6 skew and the stock -43% from its high: the asymmetry is that a guide merely matching the published bear case leaves shorts needing ten days of volume, and EPAM's +7% on a flat guide plus buyback shows the sector will pay for stabilisation; the repeated guide cuts are why it is not larger.

A floating-price convertible (lesser of $17.53 and 90% of the three lowest VWAPs, $3.86 floor) with a further $75m tranche and a vote to lift authorised shares to 200m against 27.5m outstanding is continuous supply that disarms the 17.8% short, and the release first discloses Q3 cash against $228m of equipment commitments while Q4 consensus sits above the top of the company's own guide with no confirmation the Batam go-live happened; the crowded short and a capitulated tape are the real offset.

Catena's 10-16 pre-release (-29% revenue, target dropped, blamed on generative search taking affiliate traffic) lands squarely on the third of revenue that is SEO, while the reaffirmed FY guide needs a Q4 of ~$45-50m revenue and ~$16-20m EBITDA against a record prior Q4 and the sell side has not cut; a Q3 EBITDA under ~$8.6m also puts the 3.00x covenant in play, and the only real counter is Better Collective's record +6% organic Q3 printed the evening before.

Near a non-result: almost every item is explicitly priced, and the two that are not roughly cancel — street FY27 EPS of $23.49 sits ~2% above the $22.88-23.12 guide into a company whose Q1 habit is to reiterate (the 09-17 reaffirm-only drew -4% and a downgrade), against Intuit's own QuickBooks Small Business Index showing October revenue per business +2.6% m/m, a published series no preview cites.

Keysight reaffirmed the Q4 guide on 11-02 with the books closed two days earlier and said demand is strong, Viavi's overlapping quarter showed core data-center test more than doubling with a +9% sequential guide, and Coherent guided FY27 growth above 60% on the 1.6T ramp Keysight names as its wireline driver — yet the stock fell 14% purely with the AI complex; capped because the Q1 FY27 consensus is unsourced and management has called supply 'a governor', which is exactly the Teradyne template.

18.57% of float short at 13.65 days to cover cannot exit inside the window, and a board under covenant relief raised the dividend for a 33rd year the day before the numbers, which argues against a distress print; mostly offset by a new CEO's first FY27 framework (classic reset risk) and soft funeral-volume reads from SCI and Carriage.

About $0.70 of the $11.65 FY26 guide is a non-recurring IEEPA recovery, so FY27 consensus of $12.24 — revised UP from $11.66 over 90 days — needs roughly +12% on the underlying base, and the two closest aerospace peers (TransDigm 11-10, Woodward 11-18) have just set a conservative initial-guide tone and been sold; the unannounced PAC-3 flow-down is the credible upside and is netted to ~6% of sales.

The FY guide needs Q4 daily-average comps of ~2.6-4.6% against a 4.2% lap while Sprouts comped -0.9% over the identical July-September months, and the three-analyst Q4 EPS consensus of $0.56 sits at the very top of the guide-implied range on a Q3 whose $0.48 included ~$0.06-0.07 of insurance recovery; last year's first FY guide came in ABOVE the street and the stock still fell 5%, and 5 of 7 prints have been down.

The first formal FY27 EBITDA range, from a CEO six weeks into the job, has to be set against a preliminary 'flat vs ~$1.48bn' given when management also said inflation was tracking to the high end and pricing lags into late FY27 — and Cal-Maine's 09-30 print confirmed how far egg economics fell AFTER the $500M Foodservice run rate was set; the 12-15% of float short with the stock 31% off its high is the offsetting mechanism.

Close to balanced: the ~RMB0.23 EPS bar needs operating income up ~47% q/q into a quarter management said would carry normalising margin, lower-margin distributor revenue and 49% minority leakage, but the same print first consolidates that distributor (the 2025 analogue drove +10.3%) and RLX has declared a Q3 dividend two years running, which at $1.46 with cash above market cap is a real in-window catalyst; prior misses on this name cost only ~3%.

An independent company-level series (Placer.ai same-store visits +12.3%, at or above 10% every month through October) against a +6-7% comp guide, on a tracker that read +16.4% and +17% before the last two quarters when Ross printed 10% and 17% traffic-led comps and beat its EPS guide top by wide margins — and TJX's call the day before confirms Marmaxx transactions essentially flat, i.e. Ross taking the traffic; the name has been paid for comp beats on four straight prints (6 of 7 up) and went in 8.6% below Nov 11 after lagging the off-price rebound, with fuel and the warm-weather Q4 comment the honest offsets.

Two forces that nearly cancel: 9.1 days to cover on a rising short base into a new 52-week low after -21.5% in five sessions, with the WRD 3.0 line corroborated by GAC Aion's September units and i60 orders that no US coverage carries; against a FY consensus needing H2 at twice H1 and a Q4 of RMB 513.5M with no company revenue guide at all, and a sector whose tape just sold Pony's 75% revenue beat.
